> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #241 implements issue #201’s `/skill` v1 extension protocol. It adds typed skill package resolution, optional `skill-setup.yaml` validation/execution, `skill_root` propagation, workflow setup failure handling, tests, and user-facing docs. The linked issue explicitly accepted repo-owned setup manifests but called out that Sepo must not accidentally run PR-supplied setup with agent credentials. Overall structure matches the approved plan, but one trust-boundary edge case needs fixing before merge.

## Review
The main implementation is well-scoped and mostly consistent with the repository’s workflow patterns. However, the current trust guard only denies the raw `pull_request` event and misses PR review-triggered entrypoints that also run from PR merge refs.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| PR review events can still run PR-supplied skill setup | BLOCKING | `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` sets `SKILL_SETUP_TRUSTED_REF` false only for `pull_request`, but the entrypoint also accepts `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`. Those events can run on `refs/pull/<number>/merge`, allowing review-triggered `/skill` runs to execute PR-supplied setup. |
| Setup refusal comments are too generic | WARNING | Trust refusals and real setup command failures both produce the same “setup failed / check logs” PR comment. This is not a security blocker, but it will make expected PR-ref refusals look like broken setup scripts. |
| Skill setup path docs omit absolute-path behavior | INFO | Setup steps receive `SKILL_ROOT` and `SKILL_DIR` as resolved absolute paths, but the docs only say those variables are exposed. Clarifying this would prevent skill author confusion. |

## Progress
- PR #241 already implements the approved `skill-setup.yaml` protocol, docs, CLIs, path validation, and custom `skill_root` plumbing.
- The linked issue #201 explicitly supports repo-owned executable setup, with the constraint that unreviewed PR refs must not supply setup.
- Reviewer inputs disagreed on severity: the rubrics review passed the raw `pull_request` guard, while the deeper code review found the wider PR merge-ref gap.
- Posted one inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` line 452: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/241#discussion_r3237709146
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before posting; no comments were minimized and no threads were resolved.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>PR review events can still run PR-supplied skill setup</summary>

**Cause:** The skill setup guard is `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, while `.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml` also routes `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`. Those PR review events are PR-ref contexts, so `actions/checkout` can load `.skills/<name>/skill-setup.yaml` from an unreviewed PR merge ref.

**Candidate solutions:** Base `SKILL_SETUP_TRUSTED_REF` on the checked-out ref, for example denying `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')`, or explicitly deny all PR review event types too. Add a regression test that covers `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`, not just `pull_request`.

**Comments:** This violates the issue #201 trust-boundary discussion and the new docs’ claim that unreviewed PR heads cannot supply executable setup.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Setup refusal comments are too generic</summary>

**Cause:** `run-skill-setup.js` exits failure for both trust refusals and failed setup commands, and the workflow always posts the same “Check the workflow logs for the failed setup step” message.

**Candidate solutions:** Have the CLI expose a distinct failure reason or exit code for untrusted refs, then post a specific comment such as “Skill setup cannot run from PR checkout contexts.” Keep ordinary command failures on the current setup-failed message.

**Comments:** This can be fixed with the trust-boundary patch or left as a small follow-up if maintainers want only the security fix in this PR.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Skill setup path docs omit absolute-path behavior</summary>

**Cause:** `runSkillSetup` passes resolved absolute paths for `SKILL_ROOT` and `SKILL_DIR`, while `.agent/docs/customization/skills.md` does not say whether these are absolute or repo-relative.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the docs sentence to say Sepo exposes `SKILL_NAME`, absolute `SKILL_ROOT`, and absolute `SKILL_DIR` to setup steps.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the unresolved PR-ref trust guard is concrete, security-relevant branch work and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Update the skill setup trust guard to deny all PR merge-ref checkout contexts, not only `pull_request`.
- [ ] Add regression coverage for `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment` skill setup trust handling.

You’re right in spirit: it **is** an additional GitHub Actions step.

In this PR the static Actions step is:

[`Run skill setup`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L445-L453)

That step runs:

```yaml
run: node .agent/dist/cli/run-skill-setup.js
```

The Node CLI then reads the selected skill’s `skill-setup.yaml`, validates it, checks the PR trust boundary, and executes each manifest `steps[].run` command. The `bash` in the snippet is just the default interpreter for those setup commands, similar to how GitHub Actions `run:` defaults to a shell:

[`steps[].shell` defaults to `bash`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/skills.ts#L215-L224)

So the layering is:

```text
GitHub Actions step
  -> Sepo CLI validates/resolves skill setup
    -> shell runs each repo-defined setup command
```

The reason it is not modeled as arbitrary extra Actions YAML from the skill file is that `skill-setup.yaml` is intentionally **not GitHub Actions YAML**. Docs say it supports `run`, `env`, `shell`, and timeout, but not dynamic `uses:` steps:

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/docs/customization/skills.md#L59-L61

That keeps the extension protocol small and lets Sepo do things Actions YAML alone would make awkward:

- resolve `skill_root` and `.skills/<name>` consistently;
- no-op cleanly when no setup file exists;
- validate the schema before running commands;
- block setup from PR checkout refs before any repo-provided setup command runs;
- post a controlled setup failure response before skipping the agent run.

Could this be wrapped as a composite action for readability? Yes. But internally it would still need a runner process that reads the per-skill manifest and executes its `run` commands. The important distinction is: **the workflow has one fixed setup step; the skill manifest defines the dynamic commands that step executes.**

Yes, but it depends what “additional GitHub workflow step” means.

If you mean a **fixed step in `agent-router.yml`**, then yes. That is possible, and for one hardcoded setup it is simpler:

```yaml
- name: Setup deep research skill
  if: needs.portal.outputs.skill == 'deep-research' && !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')
  run: python -m pip install agent-papers-cli
```

That would be clean for a repo that only has one or two known skills and is comfortable editing the workflow directly.

But if you mean “each skill can ship some setup YAML, and Sepo turns that into real GitHub Actions steps dynamically,” then no, not cleanly. GitHub Actions builds the job graph from the workflow file before the job runs. The workflow cannot read `.skills/<name>/skill-setup.yaml` at runtime and inject new first-class Actions steps into the same job. Also, reusable workflow callers cannot insert arbitrary steps into the middle of the called `agent-router.yml` skill job.

So the tradeoff is:

- **Static workflow step:** simpler, more native Actions UI, but every skill setup requires editing `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml`, adding conditionals, and duplicating trust/failure handling.
- **Current manifest runner:** one fixed workflow step, then Sepo loads the selected skill’s setup dynamically, validates it, applies the PR-ref guard, handles missing setup as no-op, and blocks the agent run on failure.

Current PR shape is here: [`Resolve skill package` then `Run skill setup`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L419-L453), with validation/execution in [`skills.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/skills.ts#L193-L293).

My take: a static workflow step is cleaner for a specific repo-local customization; the manifest runner is cleaner for Sepo’s general `/skill` extension protocol.

One possible polish: wrap `node .agent/dist/cli/run-skill-setup.js` in a local composite action like `./.github/actions/run-skill-setup`. That would make the workflow read more like an Actions-native step, while keeping the typed parser/trust logic in `.agent/src`.

@sepo-agent /answer

For that exact shape, no:

```yaml
run: <resolved-skill-path>/skill-setup.yml
```

`run:` does **not** mean “run this YAML as GitHub Actions steps.” It means “send this string to the shell.” So GitHub would try to execute `skill-setup.yml` as a shell command/script. A YAML file like:

```yaml
version: 1
steps:
  - name: Install helper
    run: npm install -g ...
```

is not executable by the shell.

GitHub Actions only interprets workflow YAML when the workflow is loaded, from `.github/workflows/*.yml`. It does not interpret arbitrary runtime YAML files as nested workflow steps.

There are two valid variants:

```yaml
# 1. Run an executable script
run: bash .skills/deep-research/setup.sh
```

or:

```yaml
# 2. Call a local action
uses: ./.github/actions/some-action
```

But neither gives us dynamic per-skill Actions steps from `<resolved-skill-path>/skill-setup.yml`.

For Sepo’s skill route, this is why the current PR has a fixed workflow step:

[`Run skill setup`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L445-L453)

That step calls a Sepo CLI, and the CLI is what interprets `skill-setup.yaml`:

[`parseSkillSetupManifest` / `runSkillSetup`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/skills.ts#L193-L293)

So the cleanest options are:

1. **Keep `skill-setup.yaml` as a Sepo manifest.**  
   Then Sepo needs an interpreter, which is the current Node CLI.

2. **Change the protocol to an executable script**, for example:

   ```text
   .skills/<name>/setup.sh
   ```

   and the workflow could do something closer to:

   ```yaml
   run: bash "${{ steps.check-skill.outputs.setup_path }}"
   ```

   That is simpler, but less structured: no schema validation, no per-step names, no per-step env, no typed timeout handling.

3. **Wrap the current CLI in a local composite action** for readability:

   ```yaml
   - name: Run skill setup
     uses: ./.github/actions/run-skill-setup
     with:
       skill: ${{ needs.portal.outputs.skill }}
       skill_root: ${{ inputs.skill_root }}
       trusted_ref: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/') }}
   ```

   Internally it would still call `node .agent/dist/cli/run-skill-setup.js`.

My recommendation: option 3 is the cleanest workflow presentation, but option 1 is the right underlying model if we want `skill-setup.yaml` to remain a structured Sepo extension protocol.
@sepo-agent /answer OK given this constraint, are there other ways to implement this feature more elegantly?

Yes. Given the Actions constraint, I see three realistic designs.

**Best balance: keep the manifest, wrap it in a local action**

Current PR has the right behavior, but the workflow reads a little low-level:

```yaml
- name: Run skill setup
  run: node .agent/dist/cli/run-skill-setup.js
```

That could become:

```yaml
- name: Run skill setup
  uses: ./.github/actions/run-skill-setup
  with:
    skill: ${{ needs.portal.outputs.skill }}
    skill_root: ${{ inputs.skill_root }}
    trusted_ref: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/') }}
```

The local action would internally call the same typed CLI. This keeps the workflow more Actions-native while preserving the good parts: schema validation, no-op when setup is missing, PR-ref blocking, outputs, and testable TypeScript logic.

That is probably the cleanest version of the current approach. The current insertion point is here: [`agent-router.yml#L445-L453`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L445-L453).

**Simplest protocol: replace `skill-setup.yaml` with `setup.sh`**

If we want maximum simplicity, make setup an executable script:

```text
.skills/<name>/
  SKILL.md
  setup.sh
```

Then Sepo only resolves the path and runs:

```yaml
- name: Run skill setup
  if: steps.check-skill.outputs.setup_exists == 'true'
  run: bash "${{ steps.check-skill.outputs.setup_path }}"
```

This is elegant because there is no manifest interpreter. But it gives up the structured v1 contract currently implemented in [`skills.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/skills.ts#L193-L293): named steps, per-step env, shell selection, timeout validation, and better error messages.

I would choose this only if we believe skill setup should just be “run this repo-owned script.”

**Not worth it: try to model skills as dynamic GitHub Actions**

For example:

```text
.skills/<name>/action.yml
```

and somehow:

```yaml
uses: ./.skills/${{ needs.portal.outputs.skill }}
```

This would look elegant, but GitHub Actions does not support dynamic `uses:` paths this way, and local actions require static resolution. Generating or dispatching another workflow would be much more complex, and setup would not naturally share the same job environment before `Run skill`.

So my recommendation:

- If `/skill` is meant to be a real Sepo extension protocol, keep `skill-setup.yaml`.
- Refactor the workflow call into `./.github/actions/run-skill-setup` for readability.
- Keep the parser/runner in TypeScript because that is where validation, trust rules, no-op behavior, and tests belong.
- If we decide setup does not need structure, switch the protocol to `setup.sh` instead of YAML.
